brief: Goldman's FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, the first hike since July 2023, with no dissents. GS now expects one more hike in October. The dot plot turned more hawkish, showing one additional 2026 hike and no 2027 cut, while the statement said inflation "remains elevated." Chair Warsh submitted no projections. SPX fell 45bps to 7551 post-FOMC, led down by Energy and Financials. Asset managers were net sellers ($829mm) in macro products. Hedge funds were small net buyers, favoring tech, consumer discretionary, communication services and consumer staples over macro products and financials. Global Fundamental L/S returns fell 1.1% in September (+12.1% YTD) as beta losses outweighed alpha gains (+0.2% MTD, +7.8% YTD). Gross/net leverage sit at the 55th/18th percentiles versus the past year. DM Asia is the most net-bought region on long buying. EM Asia and North America are the most net-sold, both on short selling. Goldman upgraded Sunbelt to Buy, 20% upside to price target, on a first-in-several-quarters rate improvement and non-residential stabilization, forecasting about 10% FY27 organic rental revenue growth and margin recovery driving double-digit EPS growth.
